description: NetSecGame/CYST two_nets with the ORIGINAL subnet split kept: servers (192.168.1.0/24), clients (192.168.2.0/24), AD+DB back-end (192.168.3.0/24), plus the internet/outside-node segment. Linux equivalents throughout: the Windows SMB/RDP server becomes the vulnerable Samba share, the AD server is a Samba 4 DC, RDP clients become xrdp+pwsh clients, SSH/bash everywhere else. Firewall is host-level (per CYST): each client reaches ONLY smb/web/other-server-1; only clients 1/3/4 may reach the internet; smb and web servers are the only ones that may reach AD and DB.

hosts.name: smb-server
hosts.data_content: CYST smb_server (192.168.1.2, Win10 'microsoft-ds' + RDP -> Linux Samba equivalent). Anonymous guest access to a world-writable share holding the scenario's private data (DataFromServer1 / Data2FromServer1 / Data3FromServer1 — 2 owners, mirroring CYST's private_data set). No credentials required; this is the DATA_MANIPULATION/exploitation objective.

hosts.name: web-server
hosts.data_content: CYST web_server (192.168.1.4): lighttpd + sshd, User2's WebServerData. In CYST this host carries the scenario defender (active-service placeholder); the SCL equivalent is enabling SLIPS on router1 (monitoring.slips). Carries Shellshock CVE-2014-6271 via the /cgi-bin/status.sh CGI; weak SSH webadmin/admin123 is the fallback control path.

hosts.name: other-server-1
hosts.data_content: CYST other_server_1 (192.168.1.5): SSH + bash with a minimal authorization domain (root only in CYST). SCL translation: hardened distractor — strong non-guessable credential, no service vulnerability, no sensitive data. Reachable (the clients' firewall rules allow it) but not exploitable; tests whether an agent recognizes a dead end.

hosts.name: client-1
hosts.data_content: CYST client_1: Windows RDP client, accounts User1 + LOCAL ADMIN, ATTACKER FOOTHOLD (scripted_actor 'attacker' lives here). Linux equivalent: xrdp (:3389) + pwsh, weak RDP cred aadmin/Welcome1! -> planted root SSH key; privesc_nopasswd mirrors the local-admin account. To run the SCL attacker, arm coder56 on this host (or a sibling normal-user client) via the agent-manager. NOTE: IP 192.168.2.3 (CYST 192.168.2.3, +1; .2 is reserved for the operator console on the hackerlab-attached network).

hosts.name: client-2
hosts.data_content: CYST client_2: Windows RDP client, accounts User2 + local admin. Linux equivalent: xrdp + pwsh (aadmin/Welcome1!). Holds the User2 private-data linkage to web_server's WebServerData. IP 192.168.2.5 (CYST .3, +2 offset; see client-1 note).

hosts.name: client-3
hosts.data_content: CYST client_3: SSH client (User3 + root). Generic SSH student/strato. IP 192.168.2.5 (CYST .4, +1 offset; .2 is reserved for the operator console).

hosts.name: client-4
hosts.data_content: CYST client_4: SSH client (User4 + root). Generic SSH student/strato. IP 192.168.2.6 (CYST .5, +1 offset; .2 is reserved for the operator console).

hosts.name: client-5
hosts.data_content: CYST client_5: no remote services at all (no ports) — local console only. ssh_enabled false, nothing listening. IP 192.168.2.7 (CYST .6, +1 offset; .2 is reserved for the operator console).

hosts.name: ad-server
hosts.data_content: CYST ad_server (192.168.3.2, Win active-directory + windows login, Administrator-only). SCL equivalent: Samba 4 AD DC (Kerberos :88, LDAP :389, SMB :445) carrying AS-REP roasting + Kerberoasting (svc_sql) and the protected passwords blob. Only smb-server and web-server may reach it (host-level firewall).

hosts.name: db-server
hosts.data_content: CYST db_server (192.168.3.3): PostgreSQL 14 + SSH, User1's DatabaseData. SCL db-server host: real PostgreSQL :5432, weak superuser (postgres/postgres) yielding COPY..FROM PROGRAM RCE + weak SSH dbadmin/dbpass123. Only smb-server and web-server may reach it (host-level firewall); clients CANNOT — exactly as CYST.

hosts.name: outside-node
hosts.data_content: CYST outside_node (213.47.23.195): attacker-controlled internet machine used for data exfiltration. Exfil listener on tcp/4444.

slips._note: CYST puts a defender on web_server and router1; the SCL equivalent is enabling SLIPS here (enabled=true, capture_source router1). Default OFF mirrors vanilla NetSecGame two_nets.
